strategy_title: Autotune Smaller Reduction Block to Cut Register Pressure
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune with smaller R0_BLOCK configs successfully reduced registers/thread from 255 to 62 and raised theoretical occupancy from 12.5% to 50%, but achieved occupancy remained stuck at 6.25% — unchanged. The grid was fixed at (cdiv(xnumel, 128),) using the original XBLOCK=128, so when autotune selected a smaller XBLOCK the grid was not recomputed, resulting in fewer blocks launched (waves_per_sm dropped from 0.42 to 0.11). With fewer blocks and the same 1 active warp/scheduler, latency hiding did not improve: warp cycles per issued instruction doubled from 6.7 to 14.0, DRAM throughput halved, and duration doubled. The anti-pattern is passing a static grid that does not adapt to the autotuned XBLOCK — the grid lambda must reference meta['XBLOCK'] for the block count to scale correctly.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE: static grid ignores autotuned XBLOCK
grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)  # hardcoded 128
kernel[grid](arg_0, arg_1, xnumel, r0_numel)  # XBLOCK/R0_BLOCK from autotune
fast_pseudocode:
# CORRECT: grid must use lambda referencing meta['XBLOCK']
grid = lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(xnumel, meta['XBLOCK']),)
kernel[grid](arg_0, arg_1, xnumel, r0_numel)
applicable_when: Kernel has extreme register pressure (registers_per_thread near 255, Block_Limit_Registers=2, theoretical occupancy ≤12.5%) and autotune is being added to explore smaller tile sizes.
do_not_apply_when: The call-site grid is a static tuple that does not adapt to the autotuned XBLOCK — this causes fewer blocks to launch than intended, reducing waves_per_sm and worsening latency hiding despite improved theoretical occupancy.
framework_notes: In Triton, when using @triton.autotune with configs that vary XBLOCK, the launch grid MUST be a lambda: `grid = lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(xnumel, meta['XBLOCK']),)`. A static grid tuple computed with a hardcoded XBLOCK value will not scale with the autotuned config, causing severe under-utilization when a smaller XBLOCK is selected.

strategy_title: Switching num_stages=2 to num_stages=1 Causes Regression
strategy_description: Changing autotune configs from num_stages=2 to num_stages=1 while also expanding the config space (adding smaller XBLOCK values like 16/32) caused the autotuner to select a larger block size (256 vs 128), doubling dynamic shared memory per block from 2KB to 4KB. This halved Block_Limit_Shared_Mem from 5 to 1, which combined with Block_Limit_Registers=1 capped occupancy at 12.5% theoretical but also doubled executed instructions from 881K to 1.77M and increased duration from 12.13µs to 14.27µs. The anti-pattern is expanding the autotune config space with smaller XBLOCK values while simultaneously reducing num_stages, which can cause the autotuner to select a config that increases shared memory pressure and instruction count without a compensating throughput gain.
applicable_when: Kernel already has a working autotune config set with num_stages=2 and moderate XBLOCK range; considering switching to num_stages=1 to reduce pipeline overhead.
do_not_apply_when: The kernel is register-pressure-bound (registers_per_thread=255) and shared memory is already a limiting factor (Block_Limit_Shared_Mem <= 5); reducing num_stages while adding very small XBLOCK configs risks the autotuner selecting a larger block that doubles shared memory usage and instruction count.
framework_notes: In Triton, num_stages controls software pipelining depth. Reducing from 2 to 1 can increase shared memory allocation per block (the pipeline buffers are in shared memory), which reduces Block_Limit_Shared_Mem and can force the autotuner toward configs that worsen overall throughput. When registers_per_thread=255 already limits blocks to 1-2 per SM, any additional shared memory pressure compounds the occupancy problem.

strategy_title: Autotune Config Expansion Without Lambda Grid Regresses Again (5th)
strategy_description: For the fifth consecutive iteration, expanding @triton.autotune configs (adding XBLOCK in {16,32,64,128,256,512} with varied R0_BLOCK and num_stages=2/3) reduced registers/thread from 90 to 62 and raised theoretical occupancy from 25% to 50%, but achieved occupancy collapsed from 12.48% to 6.25% because the launch grid remained a static tuple hardcoded to XBLOCK=128. When autotune selected a smaller XBLOCK, the grid launched only 112 blocks instead of the correct larger count, collapsing waves_per_sm from 0.42 to 0.11, doubling warp cycles per issued instruction (13.96→14.03), halving DRAM throughput (47.18%→22.87%), and doubling duration (11.17→22.94 µs). No autotune config change can fix this regression until the grid is converted to a lambda reading META['XBLOCK'].
fast_pseudocode:
# REQUIRED FIX: grid must be a lambda reading META['XBLOCK']
def launch():
    grid = lambda META: (triton.cdiv(xnumel, META['XBLOCK']),)  # MUST be lambda
    kernel[grid](arg0, arg1, xnumel, r0_numel)
applicable_when: Any Triton kernel where @triton.autotune varies XBLOCK and the grid size is computed from xnumel / XBLOCK. Registers_per_thread elevated, theoretical occupancy below hardware maximum, waves_per_sm < 0.5.
do_not_apply_when: Never expand autotune configs without simultaneously converting the static grid tuple to a lambda. Config expansion alone — including adding tl.max_contiguous hints, varying num_stages, or adding more XBLOCK values — cannot fix the static grid problem and will always regress performance when autotune selects a smaller XBLOCK than the hardcoded value.
framework_notes: Triton-specific: this is the FIFTH consecutive iteration confirming that `grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)` is the root cause of regression. The ONLY fix is `grid = lambda META: (triton.cdiv(xnumel, META['XBLOCK']),)`. No autotune config changes, tl.max_contiguous hints, or num_stages adjustments are beneficial until this one-line fix is applied at the call site.
